title: Whole-body Regulation & Coupling Atlas
purpose: Describe the body as coupled regulatory systems rather than isolated organs: flows, sensors, control signals, effectors, buffers, barriers and recurrent feedback loops.
epistemic_rule: This is physiology architecture for research/navigation, not diagnosis or medical advice. Symbolic correspondences belong to the Symbolic Body Crosswalk and cannot be inferred from physiology alone.

control_loop_template.example_pattern: change in state → detection → integration → autonomic/endocrine/behavioral response → changed state → new sensing

major_couplings.flow: ventilation/gas exchange → blood transport → tissue delivery/use → CO2 return
observables: oxygen content or saturation where clinically measured
major_couplings.boundary: No single organ owns oxygen delivery.

major_couplings.flow: intake/absorption → storage/release → circulating substrates → tissue use
major_couplings.boundary: Metabolic regulation is multi-organ and time-dependent.
Pressure regulation is distributed and cannot be reduced to heart function alone.

major_couplings.flow: barrier exposure → recognition → local/systemic signaling → containment/repair/memory
major_couplings.boundary: Immune activation can be protective, dysregulated or context-dependent.

major_couplings.flow: salient demand → appraisal/integration → autonomic/endocrine mobilization → recovery/adaptation
major_couplings.boundary: Stress is not one hormone or one emotional state.

major_couplings.flow: internal state → neural/humoral signals → central representation/integration → autonomic/behavioral response
major_couplings.boundary: Subjective experience and measured physiology are related but not identical.

major_couplings.flow: goal/state estimate → motor command → force/movement → sensory feedback → correction
environmental timing cues + internal clocks → phase coordination → sleep/wake and physiological rhythms
major_couplings.boundary: Pineal signaling participates in timing; it is not a solitary master clock for the whole organism.

major_couplings.flow: capillary/interstitial exchange + tissue drainage → lymph/venous return and organ-specific clearance
major_couplings.boundary: CSF, lymph, blood and interstitial fluid are distinct compartments with interfaces, not one universal river.

integration_principles: The same variable can be regulated by several systems at different timescales.
Feedback can stabilize one variable while shifting another; regulation involves tradeoffs.
A local perturbation can propagate through flows, signaling, behavior or resource competition.
Redundancy creates resilience but can hide declining reserve until stress exposes it.
The organism is open: food, air, microbes, light, temperature, social context and activity are inputs.
Health cannot be inferred from one biomarker without context, reference ranges and clinical interpretation.

project_bridge.safe_analogy: The project may compare distributed physiological regulation with House/Rooms/River/Axis architecture when the biology stays separately typed.
forbidden_shortcuts: thalamus = Father's House as anatomical fact
